ledger.note: October 1890: the Company's first Administrator takes up Mashonaland. 'The first Administrator, A. R. Colquhoun, was appointed in October 1890, soon after the Pioneer Column had arrived at Fort Salisbury'; the Royal Charter 'came into effect on 20 December 1889' and the Southern Rhodesia page has the column founding 'Fort Salisbury (now Harare) in Mashonaland'. The pages give no boundary; the wide reading of Mashonaland is the researcher's. The Rudd Concession came from Lobengula, whose dossier (ndebele-kingdom) does not hold Mashonaland; british-africa ledger 3 names ndebele-kingdom as counterpart.

region.text: Mashonaland: 'A protectorate was proclaimed by an Order-in-Council of 9 May 1891, initially covering Mashonaland and later Matabeleland'

ledger.note: 9 May 1891: the Crown proclaims a protectorate over the Company's Mashonaland, with Matabeleland following in 1894 (the gain below carries it). The Company ruled for the British government under a charter that was 'later extended for a further 10 years, thus it expired in 1924'; recorded as the colony's tie to the metropole, which should carry the matching vassal_start.

ledger.note: 1899: the Order in Council gives the Company the powers over the Lozi outer realm. 'With the 1899 Order, Lewanika lost powers over territory outside of the Valley (Bulozi proper) to the BSAC'; the Lochner concession of 1890 ('mining rights in the whole country') and the Lawley concession of 1898 precede it. A loss of powers rather than of title, as in lozi-kingdom ledger 5; the Northern Rhodesia page adds that the 9 May 1891 Order-in-Council had placed the area under BSAC administration on paper, 'but no BSAC Administrator was sent to Barotseland until 1895'. Confidence 2 (reviewer, g-af review): the page names only 'territory outside of the Valley (Bulozi proper)'; the drawn region is lozi-kingdom ledger 5's disc construction (c2 there).

wars.name: Second Matabele War
wars.outcome: Page gives the campaigns' names ('Rhodesia (1896) and Mashonaland (1897)') and no result; Company rule over both continues until 1923.
wars.note: The BSAC page says 'the Matabele and Mashona rebellions of 1896' and 'the two campaigns of the Second Matabele War'. No territory is said to have been lost, so no zone.

wars.name: Jameson Raid
wars.outcome: The Company 'unsuccessfully attempted to stage a coup in the neighbouring Transvaal Republic'; no border changed.
wars.note: The Southern Rhodesia page dates the attempt 1895; the BSAC page dates the Jameson Raid to 1896.

certainty.note: No page opened gives the Company's boundary lines. The Orders-in-Council fixed boundaries with other British territories on paper and the Anglo-Portuguese and Anglo-German treaties fixed some in North-Eastern Rhodesia (Northern Rhodesia page), but none is given as a surveyed line.

sources.title: British South Africa Company
sources.note: Charter (in effect 20 December 1889, expired 1924), first Administrator October 1890, the 9 May 1891 protectorate, Orders-in-Council 1899 and 1900, Second Matabele War, end of rule 1923 and 1924.

sources.title: First Matabele War
sources.note: October 1893 - January 1894, Bulawayo reached 3 November 1893, Lobengula's death, 'Matabeleland brought under BSAC control'.

sources.title: Barotseland
sources.note: The 1899 Order and the Company's powers outside Bulozi proper, the Lawley concession of 1898, the 1911 merger.

sources.title: Northern Rhodesia
sources.note: Order-in-Council of 9 May 1891, no administrator in Barotseland until 1895, Orders of 1899 and 1900, merger 1911, protectorate 1 April 1924, infobox area 751,925 km2.

sources.title: Southern Rhodesia
sources.note: Pioneer Column 1890 and Fort Salisbury, annexation 12 September 1923, 1 October 1923 constitution, infobox area 372,518 km2 for 1904.

notes: No Cliopatria row exists for the Company; every keyframe is new. Five pages opened. The Company is a colony in the sense of the brief (it ruled for the Crown): the matching vassal_start / vassal_end belong in the united-kingdom dossier, which has no BSAC event. Start 1890 (October) rather than the charter's 1889: the Royal Charter 'came into effect on 20 December 1889' (BSAC page) but the Company held no land until the Pioneer Column and the first Administrator of 1890. Not settled: (1) the 9 May 1891 Order-in-Council is quoted differently on two pages (BSAC: a protectorate 'initially covering Mashonaland'; Northern Rhodesia: the area of Northern Rhodesia placed under BSAC administration), and no administrator reached Barotseland before 1895, so the lands north of the Zambezi are drawn only from 1899 and 1900. (2) The Matabeleland Order-in-Council of 18 July 1894 (cited by ndebele-kingdom ledger 11) is not on the First Matabele War page. (3) The Company's treaties with chiefs, Katanga (which 'became part of the Congo Free State'), Nyasaland and Bechuanaland interests, and the Anglo-Portuguese boundary of Manica are not dated on the pages opened. (4) The year 1895 (the name 'Rhodesia' on 3 May 1895, First Matabele War page) is not an event. (5) british-africa ledger 3, 6 and 8 draw the same Rhodesian land as British Africa's; once this dossier compiles, the two overlap and one should defer. Counterparts without dossiers: southern-rhodesia (1923-1964) and northern-rhodesia (1924-1964); both flagged in the report.
